source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Decide how reproduction can create both continuity and variation in living beings.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: reproduction is the same as its neighbouring term in this chapter, so the decision does not change.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: Without reproduction, life would eventually disappear from Earth.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: continuity plus variation -> persistence of life happens first, and that produces reproduction and inherited instructions.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when Without reproduction, life would eventually disappear from Earth is not true.

intelligence.enrichment: Reproduction keeps each type of organism from disappearing; parents pass instructions to offspring, causing resemblance, while small changes in those instructions can create variation that may help survival under changing conditions. reproduction and inherited instructions -> continuity plus variation -> persistence of life The learner correctly uses the chapter relationship: Reproduction keeps each type of organism from disappearing; parents pass instructions to offspring, causing resemblance, while small changes in those instructions can create variation that may help survival under changing conditions. Reproduction only makes exact copies, so variation must come from a completely separate process.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 8 Science question. Chapter: Why Earth supports life. The student must decide: Decide how reproduction can create both continuity and variation in living beings. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Every option must be a claim that could answer the stem, and wrong options must be the same kind of answer as the key (a next term, a named process, or a row of the same shape). If the stem continues a number list, every option names a next term. Never write that naming or writing a term is what creates the list.
